images.title: Three routes to the berry
images.purpose: Show that three routes along the grid lines reach the same berry, 4 cm east and 3 cm north of the ant, and that the two routes with no step the wrong way are 7 cm while the route with a step to the west is 9 cm.
images.composition: Three identical small grids in a row, one route drawn in each in its own colour, with the legs written under each grid and its length in a chip, and one line at the bottom that names the shortest routes.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 55, the title Three routes to the berry in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). THREE SMALL GRIDS side by side, each 7 columns by 4 rows of equal squares, every square 56 by 56 px, so each grid is 392 px wide and 224 px tall and holds exactly 28 squares, with thin grey #6B7280 grid lines (2 px) and a 3 px dark #2B2B2B outline; the grids cover y 250 to 474 and x 52 to 444, x 532 to 924 and x 1012 to 1404 (left grid, middle grid, right grid). No numbers are written on the grids. In every grid the ant is at the grid point 1 square from the left edge and 1 square above the bottom edge, and the berry is at the grid point 4 squares to the east and 3 squares to the north of the ant, on the top edge. THE ANT in each grid: a small ant drawn from 3 touching dark #1F2937 circles in a row (rear 14 px, middle 11 px, head 11 px), about 38 px wide, centred at x 108, y 418 (left grid), x 588, y 418 (middle grid) and x 1068, y 418 (right grid). THE BERRY in each grid: a vermilion #D55E00 circle 36 px across, centred at x 332, y 250 (left grid), x 812, y 250 (middle grid) and x 1292, y 250 (right grid). THE THREE ROUTES, one in each grid, each drawn as a thick line (8 px) with a 24 px arrowhead where it enters the berry: ROUTE 1 in the left grid, teal #0072B2: from the ant 4 squares east to x 332, y 418, then 3 squares north to the berry at x 332, y 250 (2 legs). ROUTE 2 in the middle grid, amber #E69F00: from the ant 3 squares north to x 588, y 250, then 4 squares east to the berry at x 812, y 250 (2 legs). ROUTE 3 in the right grid, reddish purple #CC79A7: from the ant 5 squares east to x 1348, y 418, then 3 squares north to x 1348, y 250, then 1 square west to the berry at x 1292, y 250 (3 legs). HEADINGS, dark bold 36 px, centred over each grid at y 170: Route 1 at x 248, Route 2 at x 728, Route 3 at x 1208. SMALL NAMES, dark 22 px: the word ant centred at y 498 under the ant of each grid (x 108, 588 and 1068) and the word berry centred at y 214 above the berry of each grid (x 332, 812 and 1292). LEG TEXT, dark 28 px, centred under each grid and wrapped on two lines (y 548 and y 582): under the left grid 4 cm east, then 3 cm north; under the middle grid 3 cm north, then 4 cm east; under the right grid 5 cm east, then 3 cm north, then 1 cm west. LENGTH CHIPS: three white rounded rectangles 260 by 64 px at y 630 to 694, each with a 4 px outline in its route's colour and bold dark 36 px text, centred under each grid: 4 + 3 = 7 cm (teal outline), 3 + 4 = 7 cm (amber outline) and 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 cm (reddish purple outline). BOTTOM LINE: centred at x 728 and y 765, the text The shortest routes are 7 cm in dark bold 40 px. COMPASS: a compass card, a square 100 by 100 px at x 1330 to 1430 and y 20 to 120, white with a #2B2B2B outline (3 px), with N at the top (centred at x 1380, y 42), S at the bottom (x 1380, y 98), W at the left (x 1352, y 70) and E at the right in red #D55E00 (x 1408, y 70), all bold 22 px, at the top right. In all: 3 grids of 28 squares, 3 ants, 3 berries, 3 routes with 2, 2 and 3 legs, 3 headings, 3 leg texts, 3 chips, 1 bottom line, 1 compass card. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: The shortest routes go only towards the berry: 4 + 3 = 7 cm either way round, while the route with a step 1 cm to the west is 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 cm.
images.description: Three grids with an ant and a berry, showing Route 1 (4 cm east then 3 cm north, 7 cm), Route 2 (3 cm north then 4 cm east, 7 cm) and Route 3 (5 cm east, 3 cm north, 1 cm west, 9 cm).
images.context: Concept image for Finding the Shortest Route. It follows the idea of comparing routes on the ant's grid in your maths book and uses the numbers of this concept's own example, not the numbers of the book's questions.
images.teaching_notes: Let the child trace each route with a finger and add the legs. Then ask which step of Route 3 goes away from the berry. The slip to watch: choosing the route with the fewest turns instead of adding the cm.

image_decisions.why: Three routes drawn side by side with their lengths make 'the shortest route has no step the wrong way' countable, which words alone do not.
